metadata.filter_note: Only legislation with non-zero fiscal impact is included. Zero-cost and unestimable bills are excluded.

records.title: A Local Law in relation to workforce stabilization payments for school paraprofessionals, and providing for the repeal thereof

program_breakdowns.program: Workforce Stabilization Payments for School Paraprofessionals
program_breakdowns.description: Annual non-pensionable lump sum payments of $10,000 per eligible school paraprofessional, pro-rated by school days on payroll.
program_breakdowns.offset_notes: Cost may be negated or reduced if higher wages are secured through collective bargaining.

records.impact_narrative_revenue: It is anticipated that there would be no impact on revenues resulting from the enactment of this legislation.
records.impact_narrative_expenditure: It is anticipated that there would be an annualized baselined impact on expenditures of $243.9 million resulting from the enactment of this legislation, based on the headcount of paraprofessionals as of the end of Calendar Year 2025. As such, any increase or decrease to this estimate will be determined by future fluctuations in DOE's paraprofessional headcount. Higher wages secured through collective bargaining would negate or reduce the costs associated with this legislation.
records.omb_estimate_notes: The Office of Management and Budget did not provide an estimate.

records.title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring the licensing of last-mile facilities
records.effective_date: 120 days after it becomes law, except as otherwise provided by subdivision e of section 20-566.3 and subdivision a of section 20-566.4 as added by section two of this local law
agencies_full: Department of Consumer and Worker Protection

program_breakdowns.program: Personal services for investigation and enforcement
program_breakdowns.description: Support for one staff attorney and two inspectors at DCWP for additional investigation and enforcement responsibilities.

records.impact_narrative_revenue: It is anticipated that as a result of the enactment of this legislation the City would collect an additional $75,000 annually. This estimate is based on the estimate of the number of existing facilities that engage in last-mile operations and assumes the City would collect $500 for fees and licensing per business engaged in last-mile operations annually. This revenue estimate further assumes no additional revenue from fines and penalties as full compliance with the requirements of the legislation is anticipated.
records.impact_narrative_expenditure: It is anticipated that there would be additional costs resulting from the enactment of this legislation. Personal services expenditures of $257,500, including fringe, are estimated to support one staff attorney and two inspectors at DCWP for additional investigation and enforcement responsibilities. DCWP would use existing resources to comply with the remaining aspects of the legislation.
records.omb_estimate_notes: OMB did not provide an estimate.

records.title: A Local Law in relation to requiring the commissioner of health and mental hygiene to establish and operate a pilot program providing free mental health services to children who have been returned to their home following a removal, and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon the expiration thereof
agencies_full: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

program_breakdowns.program: Mental Health Services Pilot Program - Social Workers
program_breakdowns.description: Hiring of two social workers to administer mental health services to reunified children for the three-year pilot program.

records.impact_narrative_revenue: It is anticipated that there would be no impact on revenues as a result of this legislation.
records.impact_narrative_expenditure: The Council estimates that total cost of the enactment of this legislation would be $652,455 to hire two social workers to fulfill this legislation's requirements for the three-year period of the pilot. The annual salary for each social worker is estimated to be $72,495 with a 50 percent fringe rate for a total cost of $108,743 per year for each position. Because this legislation is anticipated to be effective for only a portion of Fiscal 2027, the prorated costs in that year are estimated to be $159,688. For Fiscals 2028 and 2029, the cost is estimated to be $217,485 per year. In Fiscal 2030 the cost is estimated to be $57,797, which is prorated for the portion of the year the program would be effective before it is deemed repealed. The Council estimates the pilot program would operate with 50 slots for eligible families and the two social workers to administer services. Based on the Council's analysis of current ACS operations and understanding of the removal process, youth who have been removed from their families and then reunified are typically already participating in court-mandated or other ACS-provided mental health services as part of the reunification process and the demand for this program is likely to only require the hiring of two additional social workers for the duration of the pilot.
records.omb_estimate_notes: The Office of Management and Budget did not provide an estimate.

records.title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to increasing access to data around gender-based violence
agencies_full: Mayor's Office to End Gender-Based Violence
Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

program_breakdowns.description: Two staff members to collect data and develop required reporting.

program_breakdowns.program: Personal Services - Social Workers and Research Scientist
program_breakdowns.description: 15 social workers and one research scientist for collecting and managing data.

program_breakdowns.program: Other Than Personnel Services - Data Dashboard Development
program_breakdowns.description: One-time cost to support the development of the data dashboard.

program_breakdowns.program: Other Than Personnel Services - Data Dashboard Maintenance
program_breakdowns.description: Annual cost for maintaining the data dashboard.

records.impact_narrative_revenue: The Council estimates that there would be no impact on the City's revenues from the enactment of this legislation.
records.impact_narrative_expenditure: The Council estimates this legislation would require an additional $2.6 million in Fiscal 2027 and $2.1 million in Fiscal 2028. This includes Personal Services (PS) costs of $217,000 annually for ENDGBV to hire two staff members to collect data and develop the required reporting. The prorated cost for these two positions in the first fiscal year is $195,003. Additionally, the Council estimates that there would be an annual PS expenditure of $1,757,000 to support DSS in hiring 15 social workers and one research scientist for collecting and managing data. The prorated expenditure for these positions is $1,578,893 for the first fiscal year. The Council also estimates a one-time Other Than Personnel Services (OTPS) cost of $860,000 in Fiscal 2027 to support the development of the data dashboard. Starting in Fiscal 2028, there would be an annual $120,000 expenditure for the cost of maintaining the data dashboard.
records.omb_estimate_notes: The Office of Management and Budget did not provide an estimate; however, to prepare this fiscal impact statement the Council relied upon information provided by OMB in an estimate dated October 13, 2025, in relation to Int. No. 1416-2025, which would have imposed the same requirements as this legislation.

records.title: To amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring home delivered meals to be delivered each day of the calendar year.

program_breakdowns.description: Additional meals to meet requirement of 1 meal per day, 7 days a week, 365 days per year for authorized older adults.
program_breakdowns.offset_notes: FY27 prorated amount is $16.8 million (1.2 million meals); full year impact is $22.6 million (1.5 million meals) at $14.78 per meal reimbursement rate.

records.impact_narrative_revenue: It is anticipated that there would be no impact on revenues resulting from the enactment of this legislation.
records.impact_narrative_expenditure: It is expected that the uptake rate for weekend meals in the HDM program initiated by this legislation would be similar to the current uptake rate for weekday meals. The Council anticipates that the implementation of this legislation would result in a need for approximately 1.5 million additional meals annually. At the current reimbursement rate of $14.78 per meal, the additional 1.5 million meals would cost approximately $22.6 million annually. The Council estimates that in Fiscal 2027 the prorated number of additional meals required would be approximately 1.2 million, which would cost about $16.8 million.
records.omb_estimate_notes: OMB did not provide an estimate.

No. 825-2024, which would have imposed the same requirements as this legislation.

records.title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to the installation of solar-powered crosswalks

program_breakdowns.description: Annual installation of 100 illuminated, solar-powered traffic control devices at crosswalks at an average cost of $500 per installation.
program_breakdowns.offset_notes: Maintenance to be covered by existing DOT resources.

program_breakdowns.description: One-time study regarding the efficacy of solar-powered devices in comparison with crosswalks without these devices.

records.impact_narrative_revenue: It is anticipated that there would be no impact on revenues resulting from the enactment of this legislation.
records.impact_narrative_expenditure: It is estimated that the enactment of this legislation would require an additional $10,000 per year, for a total of $50,000 over five years in Other Than Personal Service (OTPS) costs. This estimate assumes that DOT would install 100 solar installations annually, as required by this legislation, at an average cost of $500 for each solar installation. Additionally, there would be a one-time OTPS cost of $500,000 for a study regarding the efficacy of these devices in comparison with crosswalks without these devices. DOT would maintain each installation with existing resources.
records.omb_estimate_notes: The Office of Management and Budget did not provide an estimate.
